title: Rehearsing a vaudeville show and the TOBA circuit dates
summary: After the show closed in Palatka they rehearsed a week then played TOBA theatres, starting at the Eighty-One in Atlanta, a week per town, travelling by train.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Well, here's what the changes were. See, the show closed in Palatka, Florida, and we stayed there for a while. Then we got together a band and rehearsed. He rehearsed a vaudeville show. See, a vaudeville show was much different than a show on a carnival. He got that show together. Then we went on the T.O.B.A. circuit.
Right, the T.O.B.A. vaudeville circuit.
Yeah. We went on that circuit. So we opened up, and...
That's "Tough On Black Asses."
That's right. That's what the comedians made out of it, heh-heh! The first date was at the Eighty-One Theatre in Atlanta, Georgia.
How long did he rehearse the vaudeville show before he put it into vaudeville?
About a week.
So it started around that time, in November.
Phillips - 35

Yeah, we started round about November... That's right. Around Thanksgiving, somewhere around that way. Then, after we left that, our next date was Greenville, South Carolina. Then our next date was...
You played in theatres in all of these places.
All of these were in theatres, yeah. The next date was Pensacola, Florida. Our next date from Pensacola, Florida, was Columbus, Georgia.
How long did you have between Greenville and Pensacola?
All of them was a week.
You were a week in each place?
In each place, yeah.
Then how long did you have to get to the next city? Because Greenville to Pensacola is a pretty long distance?
I don't know. About a day. It ain't too long. Ain't too far. Not too far. Maybe 300-400 miles. We traveled by train...
Did you still use the Pullman...
No. We traveled on the train.
Not the Pullman car.
The Pullman car belonged to the show that we was on.
But not for the vaudeville.
No, we had tickets. Everybody went on the train. It must have been something like about 15 people on
